Chapter 10: The Ongoing Journey—Embracing Contradiction, Growth, and the “Bad Feminist” Within
You know, there’s really no finish line when it comes to the work of justice. There’s no magical moment when everything’s fixed, or when someone becomes the perfect feminist, activist, or ally.
It’s a journey that never really ends—one that’s filled with contradictions, setbacks, and fresh starts.
Picture this: a woman, years into her life as a writer and teacher, looking back at where she began. She remembers wrestling with her identity, with finding her place, and all those nagging feelings of not being “enough.” Now, she sees how she’s changed—she’s braver, more honest, and finally willing to admit when she doesn’t know something.
And yet... she’s still learning. Still stumbling sometimes. Still circling back to some of the same doubts and questions.
Somewhere else, there’s a teenager reading an essay all about “bad feminism.” And as she reads, she feels something shift. Suddenly, the pressure to be perfect isn’t so heavy. She gets that it’s okay to care about things that are messy, to make mistakes, to keep figuring stuff out. That label—“bad feminist”—turns into a badge of honesty. It’s a reminder that imperfection doesn’t mean you’re failing. It just means you’re involved, you’re trying.
Most of us never really arrive at absolute certainty. The world’s way too complicated for that, and the work is never truly finished. But if there’s one thing that stands out over time, it’s this: what matters most is the willingness to keep going. To keep asking questions. To keep caring, keep showing up, even when it’s hard.
If you ever catch yourself worrying that you’re not good enough, here’s an invitation—embrace the mess. The world needs more people who are willing to try, to fail, to learn, and then get up and try again.
The work of justice? It’s not about being pure or perfect. It’s about persistence. The most important thing is that we keep moving forward, together.
